summary: Attacked the registered leader-side gap with a new independently assessable investigation, @q-snapshot-loop, aimed at the replication responsibility rather than the follower ingest responsibility. Source Behavior added (@b-snapshot-loop-cycle): on a rejected AppendEntries the leader rewinds nextIndex to max(min(nextIndex-1, resp.LastLog+1),1); when that lands on the follower's snapshot boundary L and the leader's log has been compacted so L-1 is gone, setupAppendEntries returns ErrLogNotFound, replicateTo branches to SEND_SNAP, sendLatestSnapshot sets nextIndex=L+1, and the next append carries PrevLogEntry=L again, restoring the preconditions of the rejection with no repair. Registered experiment update-03.json (harness assurance_generated_test.go, now the two-node loop harness in the draft): server-A bootstrapped as a single-voter leader with TrailingLogs=0 takes a user snapshot at L and compacts; server-B is a Nonvoter seeded by a legal term-1 AppendEntries up to L (defect) or L-1 (control); A then AddVoter(B) and the counter of InstallSnapshot calls plus the follower's applied index is sampled at 300 ms and 1500 ms. Local construction feedback on the same harness design: control = one InstallSnapshot, follower applied index 9; defect = install_snapshot_calls_early 2675 / late 15920 with follower applied index pinned at L=8, i.e. bounded non-progress with the retry cycle, and leader commit still advancing to 9 so the claim is scoped to that follower's replication. The interpretation is recorded as conclusion=unresolved / defect_claim omitted with the counterevidence and limitations (InmemStore only, seeded rather than full-history precondition) so the measured conclusion waits for the controller's retained receipt. Structural validation returned valid=true.
